issue.title: sase_beads.md Notes And History omits @path note attachments, @@, and sase bead attach

task_type_fields.proposed_change:
The "Notes And History" section should say that inside note text `@<path>` attaches a content-addressed snapshot of that file. It should also cover:

- `@@` escapes a literal `@` that would otherwise start a reference.
- A whole-argument `@file` still reads the note's prose from that file.
- `sase bead attach <id> <file|->...` attaches files without prose.
- `sase bead attachment list|path|open` exposes the snapshots.

Make the same edit to the init template `src/sase/main/init_memory/templates/memory-sase-beads.template.md`, then republish with `sase memory init` per the memory-write policy.

Proposed by sase-1ck.10, the ga phase of epic sase-1ck (bead note attachments). The epic plan named this memory update as a follow-up, and it was confirmed during the sase-1ck landing. `sase memory read sase_beads.md` currently has no mention of attachments.

issue.creation_reason: Epic sase-1ck shipped bead note attachments GA, and its plan made the sase_beads memory update a follow-up for the land agent to file.

payload.description: Follow-up proposed during the bead note attachments epic; its plan and phases define the attachment grammar, stores, and surfaces

evidence.note: Independent confirmation from the sase-1d5 landing (master 7885562f54): the sase_beads memory still says nothing about attachments, and since sase-1d5 GA it should also point to the attachment visibility guidance (ga PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP #3 from sase-1d5.8). Attachments get an automatic audience (clean workspace files go public, uncertain ones private); agents pass -K/--private for anything sensitive, never pass -W/--public, and offer 'sase bead attachment publish' through /sase_gate; private protects bytes, not names or prose. The canonical text is in sase bead onboard, the attach/note --help epilogs, and src/sase/xprompts/skills/sase_new_task.md. Apply the same edit to src/sase/main/init_memory/templates/memory-sase-beads.template.md.
